title: Rational canonical form (Frobenius normal form) formalization

problemStatement.plain: Formal mathematical investigation: Rational canonical form (Frobenius normal form) formalization.

currentState.focus: Phase 1 (companion-matrix building block) completed via PR #9500: aeval_companionMatrix, minpoly_companionMatrix, charpoly_companionMatrix all proved. Phase 2 (full RCF: Smith normal form + block diagonal + uniqueness) is open and not started.
blockers: Phase 2: Smith Normal Form for F[X]-matrices is not in Mathlib in a directly usable matrix-diagonalization form; ~800 LOC adaptation required.
currentState.nextAction: Phase 2 forward levers (any of three viable): (A) Smith Normal Form for F[X]-matrices, ~800 LOC, largest payoff; (B) xI - A characteristic matrix construction, ~200 LOC, prerequisite for (A); (C) block diagonal similarity assembly via sibling slug composition, ~300 LOC. Each lever is large enough for its own slug or S-PREP plan.

knowledge.progressSummary: PHASE-1-COMPLETE: companion-matrix properties (aeval, minpoly, charpoly) all proved in main file with 0 sorries / 0 axioms. Main file 397 LOC, 12 theorems + 1 def. PHASE-2-OPEN: full RCF (Smith normal form + xI-A construction + block diagonal + uniqueness) requires ~1500-1800 LOC and is not started. Aristotle companion has 12 dischargeable Mathlib-API stubs (not gaps in main proof).
builtItems: companionMatrix: def for d×d companion from monic polynomial (PROVED)
aeval_companionMatrix: p(C(p))=0 via orbit cancellation argument (PROVED)
minpoly_companionMatrix: minpoly F (C(p)) = p via orbit independence + degree bound (PROVED)
charpoly_companionMatrix: (C(p)).charpoly = p via minpoly|charpoly with same degree (PROVED)
companionMatrix_linear: C(X - c) = [c] (1×1 base case, PROVED)
companionMatrix_col: column structure for non-last columns (PROVED)
Private helpers: sum_mulVec', sum_smul_pi_single, aeval_eq_sum_pow, pow_d_mulVec_e0, aeval_commute_pow, aeval_companionMatrix_mulVec_e0 (all PROVED)
insights: Companion matrix C(p) has 1s on subdiagonal, negated coefficients in last column
Mathlib lacks a direct companion-matrix charpoly/minpoly theorem at the time of Phase 1; main file fills this gap
Orbit argument: C(p)^k·e₀ = eₖ gives standard basis from cyclic action; then p(C(p))·e₀ = 0 by last-column cancellation (avoids cofactor-expansion approach)
Module-theoretic approach avoids determinant computation entirely: orbit independence → deg(minpoly) ≥ d → minpoly = p → charpoly = p

Phase 1 uses Mathlib bearers directly: minpoly.dvd, Matrix.minpoly_dvd_charpoly, Matrix.charpoly_monic, Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim, Matrix.isIntegral, Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd, Polynomial.Monic.of_mul_monic_left

Full RCF (Phase 2) needs Smith Normal Form for F[X]-matrices (~800 LOC main blocker) + xI - A characteristic matrix (~200 LOC) + block diagonal assembly (~300 LOC) + uniqueness (~200 LOC) for ~1500-1800 LOC total

Circular dependency in original Phase 1 proof plan (aeval depended on charpoly which was a sorry) was fixed by proving aeval directly via orbit argument; aeval→minpoly→charpoly ordering eliminates the cycle

Aristotle companion file's 12 sorries are intentional external-proof-search stubs; most are direct Mathlib API restatements (minpoly.dvd, Matrix.minpoly_dvd_charpoly, Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim, map_mul, map_one). They do not gate Phase 1's correctness.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.SmithNormalForm currently provides Submodule.smithNormalForm in module-theoretic form, not the matrix-diagonalization theorem with explicit invariant factors for F[X]-matrices (Phase 2 blocker)
nextSteps: Phase 2 Lever A (largest): formalize Smith Normal Form for F[X]-matrices — elementary row/column operations, polynomial Euclidean algorithm, diagonalization theorem. ~800 LOC; new slug or S-PREP plan.
Phase 2 Lever B (prerequisite): formalize the xI - A characteristic matrix map Mₙ(F) → Mₙ(F[X]); prove invariant-factor equivalence. ~200 LOC; depends on Lever A's invariant-factor definition.

Phase 2 Lever C (independent): compose with sibling slug cayley-hamilton-reduction-oq-01-oq-02 (block-matrix, 0 sorries) for block diagonal similarity assembly. ~300 LOC; may be tractable before Lever A.

(Optional, lower priority) Aristotle companion: discharge 12 stubs via direct Mathlib API; this is Aristotle's intended workload and should not be done manually unless the proof-search queue is empty.
